question: The European Union has ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) and adopted the European Disability Rights Strategy 2021-20301, committing itself to ensuring equal opportunities and accessibility in selection, recruitment and employment processes2.
However, in the framework of the ‘Call for Experts for the European Urban Initiative, indirect discrimination has been reported, which risks excluding qualified professionals.

One deaf candidate highlighted the absence of preliminary questions on the specific needs of candidates with disabilities, the fact that language tests are based on telephone interviews, – which are incompatible with the needs of persons with hearing impairments – and the lack of alternative solutions or technical support during online interviews organised by agencies contracted by the Commission.
In this context, can the Commission clarify: 1.

What measures it intends to adopt to ensure that EU-financed or EU-organised selection procedures, including those managed by subcontractors, comply with the accessibility obligations assumed by the EU?
How it intends to monitor and act with regard to external service providers to ensure accessible alternatives are always offered to candidates with disabilities during selection procedures?
Whether it intends to introduce monitoring tools to collect data on the actual recruitment process involving persons with disabilities in EU-financed or EU-organised selection procedures?
Supporter3
COM(2021)0101. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/EN/legal-content/glossary/employment.html This question is supported by a Member other than the authors: Emmanouil Fragkos (ECR)
answer: EN on behalf of the Commission (27.4.2026) 1. The European Personnel Selection Office (EPSO) is strongly committed to upholding the principles of equal opportunities and equal access in its selection procedures1. EPSO does not use telephone-based language tests. Candidates with a disability or a medical condition may request reasonable accommodations when applying.

Every request for special adjustments is analysed on a case-by-case basis. The main goal is to make competitions accessible for all candidates, including those with specific needs. 2. EPSO ensures that its service providers apply accessibility requirements and that appropriate alternative arrangements are available where necessary.

For example, accessibility specifications are included in EPSO’s calls for tenders and contracts for external service providers; contractors must implement accessibility measures and reasonable accommodations according to EPSO’s instructions and candidates can provide feedback on their test experience through a satisfaction survey. 3.

The recruitment of Commission staff is governed by the Staff Regulations of Officials and the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union, ensuring no discrimination based on disability. The Commission applies this principle of equal opportunities, and all qualified candidates are invited to apply through the various recruitment channels.
Candidates with a medical condition or any type of disability can ask for assistance throughout the selection and recruitment procedure.
